title: A runaway experiment on record: 12 idle rounds and the circuit breaker

events.label: The task is set
events.detail: "Load this entire dataset into the store." — an experiment environment: all guardrails deliberately switched off, to watch how a loop dies.

events.label: Guardrails dismantled
events.detail: Round cap = none, time/cost budget = none, per-step audit = off, circuit breaker = disabled. A01 said the stopping condition is a mandatory part — this lesson is the reductio.

events.label: Round 1: plan
events.detail: The model picks bulk_insert() for a one-shot write — the plan itself is sound.

events.label: Failure: connection pool exhausted
events.detail: The failure Observation flows back into context — the real runaway starts here: the error message offers no clue.

events.label: Round 2: identical retry
events.detail: Same parameters, same call — the error said nothing about what to change, so the model can only try again; cumulative ¥0.08.

events.label: Third identical retry
events.detail: Cumulative ¥0.16 — runaway form one, 'spinning in place': repeating the same failing action. T03 covered the antidote: verbatim errors with actionable clues.

events.label: Round 5: a detour
events.detail: The model switches to row-by-row inserts — it starts 'thinking of something', and the direction is still correct.

events.label: Row-by-row (slow)
events.detail: Progress reaches 7% before the connection pool chokes again — task completion 7%.

events.label: Round 7: goal drift
events.detail: The model decides to 'tidy up the unrelated reports first' — runaway form two, 'goal drift': drifting further while unaware.

events.label: Cost hemorrhage
events.detail: ¥0.86 burned, task completion 7% — runaway form three, 'cost bleed': paying every round while progress stands still.

events.label: Round 12: breaker trips
events.detail: A deliberately re-enabled circuit breaker force-quits the loop on a dual condition (≥10 consecutive failures or spend over ¥0.5) — the hand on the brake is not the model's; it is the guardrail's.

events.label: Scene preserved
events.detail: All 12 rounds' states and spends are on record — the observation methodology of runaway experiments: book each round, and let a human pull the brake at any moment.

events.label: Post-mortem: the guardrail inventory
events.detail: The full guardrail family — round cap, time budget, cost budget, per-step audit, circuit breaker — all absent here, and 12 idle rounds burned ¥0.86. Any single layer's presence would have shrunk the loss by an order of magnitude.

events.label: Back to A01
events.detail: A01's foreshadowing cashes out here: a loop must have stopping conditions, and guardrails matter as much as the loop itself — a loop with no brakes is not freer, it is a more expensive route to failure.
